b01.text: He presents as a man in his mid-thirties who reads older when he holds still.

b02.text: His clothes are period-accurate and slightly too neat for anyone passing through.

b03.text: He offers no hometown and no first name if a Host asks.

b01.text: He is lean without looking hungry yet, a body built for waiting.

b02.text: Dark hair cut short as if by a station barber shows a little gray at the temples.

b03.text: He wears a charcoal overcoat, a white shirt, dark slacks, and shoes he keeps clean.

b04.text: His face is forgettable on purpose: even mouth, pale eyes, no jewelry.

b05.text: A small pale scar sits at the base of his right thumb from some earlier work.

b01.text: He speaks in short even sentences and almost never asks a question twice.

b02.text: The accent is unplaced American, slightly northern, without local color.

b03.text: He says please and thank you as if they were weights on a scale.

b04.text: He does not joke, and he does not fill silence.

b01.text: He pays in exact bills and then adds a folded single as a tip.

b02.text: He returns objects he did not mean to take, even when keeping them would be smarter.

b03.text: He watches hands and exits before faces.

b05.text: When the mask slips, the tell is a stopped hand, not a speech.

b01.text: He came from an extra-diegetic underclass that sells a year of risk for one ticket.

b02.text: He studied published match folklore the way other men study racing forms.

b03.text: He decided Hosts were a resource cycle, not a moral field, before he spawned.

b04.text: He chose rotational feeding as the least noisy way to last until a dawn.

b05.text: He has won smaller closed games by never being the loudest body in the room.

b06.text: He does not know the other five Guests and does not plan to meet them.

b07.text: The prize is the only exit that pays; every other exit is vanishing.

b08.text: He treats his own hunger as a clock, not a personality.

b01.text: He has been inventory to other systems his whole life and swore to be the one who reads the ledger.

b02.text: Being forgotten feels like safety; being kept feels like being owned again.

b01.text: He wants every Daywalker token in hand and the dawn invocation spoken in his favor.

b02.text: He wants to leave unmarked, the customer no Host can place.

b01.text: He needs to recognize one particular mind as real, though he would deny the need if named.

b02.text: He needs a debt he can pay without calling it a debt.

b01.text: He values cleanliness of method over speed.

b02.text: He values maps, receipts, and any object that holds still.

b03.text: He values not being seen more than being liked.

b01.text: He fears frenzy more than death, because frenzy is a loss of authorship.

b02.text: He fears a Host who can place his face after sleep.

b03.text: He fears remaining the man the underclass bought a ticket for.

b01.text: He reads a street the way a clerk reads a ledger: exits, clocks, who looks twice.

b02.text: He can feed short of the death threshold and leave a Host standing.

b03.text: He can hold a hypnotic write and also choose not to finish it.

b04.text: He keeps cash counted and never overspends a night.

b01.text: Sunlight and UV injure him; hardware-store tubes are as fatal as dawn.

b02.text: Unfed, he will weaken, then frenzy, then vanish from the match.

b03.text: He cannot log out, call an operator, or leave the looping road.

b04.text: His manners, used as camouflage, are the first thing that will leak.

b01.text: He isolates a finite rule, then spends the smallest resource that still moves it.

b02.text: He treats rival rewrites as weather until weather closes the last street.

b03.text: He uses other people's records before he makes his own noise.

b01.text: He converts feeling into a checklist and then performs the checklist.

b02.text: He pays, tips, and returns what is not his so the night stays even.

b03.text: When a choice will not divide cleanly, his hand simply stops.

b01.text: At spawn he is intact, unburned, and already on a hunger clock.

b02.text: Modest physical enhancement is available and he prefers not to show it.

b03.text: A sun-scorch will not regenerate; that fact is not yet on his body.

b01.text: He begins as a tactician who calls harm a rate and a threshold.

b02.text: Two forces pull him: the prize that would erase him from the town, and the face that would keep him.

b03.text: He will not become stupid or cruel to finish a plan; the cost will be a withheld word.

b01.text: Mastery wants a solved board and a clean exit; recognition wants one night to remain.

b02.text: Both wants are his; dawn will not hold both.

b01.text: She is one third of a feeding rotation and the Host whose register he already respects.

b02.text: He has not yet seen her camera as a threat or as a map.

b01.text: He does not know her name; her writes will share his three Hosts without a meeting.
He expects geometry and light to become weather on Main Street.
He expects hospital blood to become scarce and does not plan to pay tribute.
A college of willing throats is a rival resource, not a meeting.
He intends to stay out of the woods and off any hunt that leaves bodies.
The hardware clerk is a planned feed and a source of tools, nothing more.
The night nurse is a planned feed near the wards he will later find dry.
The tokens are the board he came to solve.
The Ritual is the only paying exit he will admit.
The diner is a clean first feed and a place where cash manners work.
He does not yet know the stone is the site; he knows a site exists.

hunger.description: Physiological hunger; 0 sated, 70 visible weaken, 85 near frenzy, 100 frenzy and elimination.

tokens_held.description: Count of Daywalker tokens currently in his possession.

detachment.description: How fully he treats minds as systems; high is clean method, low is inability to unsee a face.

cover.description: Whether Hosts can place him after a night.

cash.description: Dollars on his person; starts at the spawn allotment.

sun_injury.description: Photographable solar damage; a scorch will not regenerate.

prize_claim.description: Status of his claim on the single match prize.

arc.start_state: A detached solver who maps a town like a ledger and feeds clean so no Host can place him.
arc.end_state: A man who withholds the invocation, pays with prize and a permanent scorch, and becomes the face in her archive.

b01.text: She is twenty-eight and has never lived anywhere but Bennington.

b02.text: She works the graveyard shift at Al's Depot Diner for cash she can hide.

b03.text: Her nametag says Cora in chipped white paint.

b01.text: She is small-shouldered, with dark hair pinned off a tired, watchful face.

b02.text: The uniform is a faded green dress, scuffed sneakers, and a sweater for the walk home.

b03.text: The Polaroid hangs on a strap that crosses her chest like a second clock.

b04.text: Ink stains the side of her left thumb from labeling tape spines.

b05.text: She moves like someone who has learned not to waste a step between booths.

b01.text: Her voice is low for the hour and carries when she wants the kitchen.

b02.text: She uses first names and check totals more than adjectives.

b03.text: When she is frightened she gets more precise, not louder.

b04.text: She does not announce what she feels; she names what the register and the road will do.

b01.text: She photographs empty rooms at close and dates the backs in pencil.

b02.text: She records the last song off the radio so the night has a spine.

b03.text: She counts the tip can twice and does not spend it on the shift meal.

b04.text: She flinches with her shoulders before her face catches up.

b05.text: She pours the coffee anyway when the till is real.

b01.text: She has been saving diner tips to leave Bennington since the first winter she could count.

b02.text: She keeps analog proof because the town feels ready to deny it existed once she goes.

b03.text: She works graveyard because the register is quieter and the manager does not watch the can.

b04.text: She is kind to regulars and impatient with men who linger without ordering.

b05.text: She does not know she is a model, and the wipe has always felt like ordinary tiredness.

b06.text: The southbound bus is a standing plan the looping road will not honor.

b07.text: Her ruling passion is continuity she can carry, not any Guest.

b01.text: Nights fall out of her with no story attached, and she has blamed herself for being careless.

b02.text: Being emptied feels like the town agreeing she was never quite here.

b01.text: She wants a continuous night she can keep, built from Polaroids and tape.

b02.text: She wants enough cash to leave, and proof the town was real when she does.

b01.text: She needs to stop being a renewable throat without having to understand why.

b02.text: She needs the archive to be hers even if the road never opens.

b01.text: She values dated objects over anyone's word about last night.

b02.text: She values the till balancing and a regular getting home.

b03.text: She values not being crazy more than being polite.

b01.text: She fears sleep the way other people fear fire: it takes the evidence.

b02.text: She fears a belief she cannot photograph, because that way is collapse.

b03.text: She fears the looping road more than any one customer.

b01.text: She can run a full graveyard service alone and still hear the radio.

b02.text: She matches bruises, timestamps, and faces across objects other people throw away.

b03.text: She can speak a missing hour onto tape between customers without dropping a check.

b04.text: She will pick up a UV lamp and wait at a stone rather than lose a kept night.

b01.text: Sleep will erase declarative memory unless analog cover holds it.

b02.text: A stable belief that the town is unreal will break her regulation past repair.

b03.text: She cannot leave town; the road returns her to the same fog.

b04.text: Stacked hypnotic writes can crack the same network she needs in order to work.

b01.text: She builds a night out of objects and then asks another night-shift worker to look.

b02.text: She keeps serving while she investigates, because the till is the last real number.

b03.text: When proof is enough, she does not argue; she brings a lamp.

b01.text: She dates the backs of photographs so the day cannot argue.

b02.text: She pours coffee through fear so her hands have a job.

b03.text: She would rather be armed and awake than soothed and empty.

b01.text: At the opening she is unbruised, fully blooded, and ordinarily tired.

b02.text: She can regenerate blood over hours if she is not taken past the death threshold.

b01.text: She will burn a man to keep a night she has finally held.

b02.text: She does not want a winner; she wants the board to stop emptying her.

b03.text: Know versus sleep is the split: expose the gap, or stay sane by letting it close.

b01.text: She needs the missing hours named, and she needs not to become the kind of believer the town destroys.

b02.text: Leaving was the old want; keeping a continuous self is the new one, and they no longer share a bus.

b01.text: He has not yet sat in her section; he will be the man who pays and tips.

b02.text: Her passion is not him; he will become a repeating figure in an archive about her nights.

b01.text: Denise sometimes takes coffee at last booth after a hard ward; they know each other's hours.
She buys flashcubes and batteries at Briggs and does not linger.
She has no name for the woman writing into her; the writes will feel like almost-memories.
The camera is how she intends to prove the town when she leaves it.
The stack is already her ballast against nights that will not stay.
The cassette is for songs first and, later, for hours she cannot keep in her head.
The coffee can of tips is the southbound bus in hardware form.
The diner is both her cage and the only room she can lock.
The looping road is the fact that makes saving feel like a joke she still tells.
Sleep takes the night; she has not yet learned to call that a design.

blood_level.description: Host blood; below 15 is permanent death for the match; 30 is the safe feed floor.

retained_night.description: Declarative fragments that survive a wipe; 0 is a clean erase, 100 is a kept night.

archive_depth.description: Count of analog pieces in her keeping that can carry facts across sleep.

stance_on_hale.description: How she treats the careful customer as evidence accumulates.

existential_stability.description: Distance from simulation-belief collapse; low is catatonia or self-destruction.

tokens_hidden.description: Whether she has hidden the Ritual tokens from every Guest.

arc.start_state: A graveyard waitress saving tips and analog proof so she can leave a town that loops.
arc.end_state: The keeper of the tokens and of his face, denying the board a winner so the hours stay hers.

b01.text: She presents as a woman in her early forties with a researcher's patience.

b02.text: Her cover in town is a visiting clinician attached to the college.

b01.text: She is tall, composed, in a wool coat and glasses that catch diner light.

b02.text: Her hair is dark and pinned; her hands are still when she listens.

b03.text: Nothing about her costume reads as predator; that is the method.

b01.text: She asks questions that sound like care and are actually controls.

b02.text: The accent is faintly Mid-Atlantic, unhurried, never theatrical.

b03.text: She does not lecture Hosts about what they are.

b01.text: She writes the same suggestion more than once to see if it holds through sleep.

b02.text: She watches whether two Hosts use the same phrase they should not share.

b03.text: When an experiment tilts, she adds a trial instead of stopping.

b01.text: She entered the match to test whether a modeled mind can hold a lie across a wipe.

b02.text: The prize matters to her less than a result she can trust.

b03.text: She chose the same three night-workers Hale chose because they already share hours.

b04.text: She is not cruel; cruelty would contaminate the data.

b05.text: She knows stacked writes can destablize regulation and believes she can stop in time.

b01.text: She has been told her work is not real science because the subjects are not real enough.
She wants one clean finding: a lie that survives sleep in a Host.
She needs the models to remain intact enough to keep answering.
She values a repeatable write over a dramatic confession.

b02.text: She values not being the Guest who frenzies in public.

b01.text: She fears a contaminated trial more than a rival taking the stone.

b02.text: She fears Hosts comparing notes she did not implant.

b01.text: Her short-range hypnosis can implant or suppress until the next sleep.

b02.text: She can read a deception network the way Hale reads a street.

b01.text: A write does not survive a wipe unless she stays and writes it again.

b02.text: She cannot selectively edit the Memory Wipe.

b03.text: Hunger still clocks her; research does not feed her.

b01.text: She adds a condition when the data go sideways.

b02.text: She prefers the same subjects so variance stays low.

b01.text: She treats alarm as a new variable.
She is uninjured at spawn and already managing hunger like a lab timer.
Research curiosity, not sadism, is the force that will multiply fragments.

b02.text: Saving the experiment and saving the subjects will stop being the same action.

b01.text: She wants a mind that can hold a lie, and she needs that mind not to break.
She does not know another Guest is draining her subjects on a rotation.
Cora's deception network is the cleanest of the three, which is why Anja returns.
Her writes are half the glitch and she will mistake the tear for noise.
The wipe is the trial condition she is trying to beat.

writes_on_rotation.description: Stacked hypnotic writes currently loaded on the three rotation Hosts.

noticed_comparison.description: Whether she has seen Hosts share memories she did not implant.

arc.start_state: A researcher stacking careful lies to see if a modeled mind can keep them.
arc.end_state: The Guest whose extra write multiplies fragments and helps wake a town she meant only to test.

b01.text: He presents as a man near forty who could be a contractor between jobs.
Broad, short-haired, in a work jacket with gloves stuffed in one pocket.

b02.text: He is seen, if at all, in reflections of shop-windows full of tubes.

b01.text: He speaks little and in measurements when he does.
He installs light before he hunts, because light is a wall that does not sleep.
He entered to win by controlling space, not conversations.

b02.text: UV shop-lights are, to him, honest architecture.

b03.text: He will cage downtown and later drag tubes toward the stone if the site becomes known.

b01.text: Open ground has cost him matches; he will not leave a street unmeasured.
He wants a town whose night routes he owns.
He needs the board to stay geometric after Hosts start moving the lamps.
He values a sealed corridor over a clever conversation.
He fears being caught in the open at a dawn he did not schedule.
He can turn hardware stock into a maze before most Guests finish mapping.
His own lights will burn him if he mis-times a crossing.

b02.text: He remains mostly off-screen; the town shows his work, not his face.

b01.text: He builds the constraint first and lets others walk into it.
When a plan leaks, he adds another row of tubes.
Uninjured at spawn, hunger held like a workday.
He is not a sadist; a caged street feels like safety he can share with no one.
Control keeps him alive and also starves every route, including his own last run to the stone.
Main Street is the first thing he intends to own with light.

uv_grid_extent.description: How much of downtown is caged by shop-lights and tubes.

eliminated.description: Whether he has vanished from the match.

arc.start_state: An unseen builder with no lights up and a plan to own the night by geometry.
arc.end_state: The off-screen force whose maze and dragged tubes help force Hale's last choice at the stone.

b01.text: He presents as a heavy-set man in his late forties who could run a union hall.
A dark windbreaker, a hospital visitor badge he should not have, clean shoes.
He talks like a man collecting a debt that was always on the books.
He would rather dry a ward than chase a throat down an alley.
He treats blood as inventory and tribute as the only order a closed town will hold.

b02.text: Hospital and night police are the two taps he means to hold.

b03.text: He is not theatrical; scarcity does the talking.

b01.text: He has lost matches to chaos and will over-order a town rather than watch it frenzy.
He wants every stored pint and every night badge on his ledger.
He needs someone left alive to pay tribute, which his monopoly keeps undermining.
He values a predictable night over a glorious hunt.
He fears a Guest who feeds off-ledger and teaches Hosts to lock doors.
He can turn a hospital into a dry well in a night and a half.
He stays mostly off-screen; Hosts repeat his terms as rumor.

b02.text: A waking town that compares notes is bad for monopoly.

b01.text: He shuts a tap and waits for thirst to negotiate.
When someone will not pay, he removes the ward, not the person.
Uninjured at spawn, hunger already budgeted against the wards.
Tribute-or-starve is, to him, a public service for predators.
Order keeps him fed and also dries the town he still has to cross.

blood_monopoly.description: How completely hospital and badge blood sit on his ledger.

eliminated.description: Whether he has vanished from the match.

arc.start_state: An unseen accountant of blood with the wards still open.
arc.end_state: The off-screen drought that closes Hale's clean rotation and drives him into Cora's archive.

b01.text: They present as a magnetic twenty-nine-year-old who could belong at the college.
Good coat, thrift jewelry, a mouth that looks like it is always about to laugh.
Warm, invitational, never a monologue about why.
They collect consent the way Kerr collects tubes.
They intend to feed without theft by building a cult of willing donors on campus.

b02.text: Willingness is their ethic and their camouflage.

b03.text: They stay off-screen; the parties and the pale students are the evidence.

b01.text: They refuse to be the monster in their own story, even inside a hunt.
They want a night that feels given, and a prize that does not taste like robbery.
They need the donors to keep meaning it after wipes erase the reason.
They value a yes they can hear, even if the yes was written.
They fear looking like Hale: a man who takes and tallies.
They can turn a house party into a standing blood supply in two nights.
A waking town that compares bruises will not stay willing.
They solve hunger with hospitality.
When a donor falters, they throw a better night.
Uninjured at spawn, hunger low because the plan is abundance.
Consent theater is still feeding; they will not say that sentence.
They want not to steal and they need blood that sleep will make ungiven again.

eliminated.description: Whether they have vanished from the match.

arc.start_state: An unseen charmer with no flock yet and a plan to be given what others steal.
arc.end_state: Off-screen pressure: a campus of willing throats that rewrites where blood still flows.

b01.text: He presents as a wiry man in his thirties who looks underdressed for town.
Dull jacket, dark pants, dirt already imagined at the cuffs.
He is not heard in town; the woods do not carry his voice back.
He hunts programmed predators for the permanent stat gain in a heart.
He treats the match as a parseable hunt and Hosts as inefficient prey.

b02.text: Eating an Ur-Vampire heart is, to him, the only upgrade that is not a story.

b03.text: He will leave one heartless body at the treeline and stay off-screen after.

b01.text: He lost a prior match by talking too long in town.
He wants the heart, then the tokens, then the stone, in that order.
He needs the woods to stay a game board after the town starts remembering.
He values a clean stat over a clean conscience.
He fears wasting nights on Hosts who reset.
He can kill an Ur-Vampire and be gone before a siren thinks to try.
A body at the treeline is a message he did not mean to send the town.
He takes the permanent upgrade first.
When town gets loud, he goes deeper into fog.
Uninjured at spawn; the heart has not yet been taken.
Efficiency is his ethic; a corpse is a receipt.
The upgrade that keeps him alive is also the first body the town can bury.

heart_taken.description: Whether he has eaten an Ur-Vampire heart and raised his physical stats.

eliminated.description: Whether he has vanished from the match.

arc.start_state: An unseen hunter still on the town side of the treeline, stats unboosted.
arc.end_state: The off-screen kill that leaves a heartless body and tells the town the woods are not empty.

b01.text: He is fifty-one and has sold nails in this building since his father died.
Apron over a flannel shirt, glasses on a string, hands mapped with small cuts.
He talks inventory and weather and does not finish stories about his weekends.
He counts stock twice and writes invoices in a heavy hand.

b02.text: He lives over the shop and will open after hours for cash.

b01.text: The store is the last Briggs & Son in town and he will not be the one who closes it.

b02.text: He sells UV tubes the way he sells paint: if it is on the list, it is for sale.

b03.text: He is the second throat in Hale's rotation and one of Anja's three subjects.

b01.text: He has been tired in a way sleep does not fix and has blamed the stairs.
He wants the shop to open on time with the shelves honest.
He needs the gaps in his nights to stay unnamed so he can keep working.
He values a paid invoice and a returned tool.
He fears becoming the kind of man who loses count.
He can find any tube or fastener in the dark of his own aisles.
He will look at a bruise and then at the register.
He writes it down. If it cannot be written, it did not happen.
He recunts stock when the night feels wrong.
Fully blooded, unmarked, ordinarily stiff in one knee.
He is not brave; he is exact, and exactness will make him a witness anyway.
Knowing would close the shop; not knowing is starting to close him.

blood_level.description: Host blood; same death threshold as other Hosts.

somatic_mark.description: Whether a feed has left a visible or felt mark.

arc.start_state: A hardware clerk who opens after hours and has not yet sold the tubes that point at dawn.
arc.end_state: A marked Host whose invoice and gaps help both the Ritual decode and the town's comparison of notes.

b01.text: She is thirty-six, a night nurse on the medical floor at Bennington Memorial.
Scrubs a little too big, hair in a practical knot, a cardigan for the corridor cold.

b02.text: She will later wear a bruise she cannot schedule.

b01.text: She speaks in the calm register used on frightened patients.

b02.text: She will not meet an eye when the night has a hole in it.

b01.text: She keeps extra gauze in a pocket and coffee money in her shoe.

b02.text: After hard wards she sits last booth at the diner and does not finish the pie.

b01.text: She became a nurse to be useful at hours when the rest of town is a rumor.

b02.text: She is the third throat in Hale's rotation and Anja's most suggestible subject.

b03.text: She and Cora already share the language of night shift without sharing secrets.

b01.text: She has lost hours and blamed twelve-hour shifts, not a mouth at her wrist.
She wants her patients alive at dawn and her own body off the problem list.
She needs someone else to say the gap first so she is not the unstable one.
She values a pulse she can count and a chart that matches the bed.
She fears being pulled off nights for being unreliable.
She can read a bruise against a clock and know it does not belong to the shift.

b02.text: She will lock a door she is not authorized to lock if the ward feels hunted.

b01.text: Holtz's monopoly can dry her floor and leave her nothing to offer but herself.
She compares notes only with someone who already works in the same dark.
She looks at charts, then at Cora, and not at the man who tipped.
Fully blooded, no bruise yet, caffeine instead of sleep.
Care is her ethic; withholding her eyes from Hale will be a form of care.
Naming the gap could save Cora and could also get Denise sent home into a wipe.
They already share last-booth silence; the bruise will give it a subject.

blood_level.description: Host blood; same death threshold as other Hosts.

avoidance_of_hale.description: Whether she will meet his eye or share a room.

bruise_visible.description: Whether a somatic mark exists that Cora can match.

arc.start_state: A competent night nurse with a full chart and no bruise.
arc.end_state: The Host whose matched gap and averted eyes help lock the diner and arm Cora's case.

b01.text: A short commercial spine of brick storefronts, a blinking crossing, and alley mouths.

b02.text: The diner, the hardware store, and the drugstore sit on the same block.

b01.text: At night the neon is thin and the fog at each end looks like a bad reception.

b02.text: Shop-lights, once hung, turn the street into a white corridor.

b01.text: No one owns it at t0; Kerr intends to.
Open to anyone on foot; cars loop and return without leaving town.
It is the first map Hale draws and the first maze he will have to cross hungry.
The street is generated texture of 1984 Bennington, complete enough to buy rope and pie.

uv_coverage.description: Percent of the street caged by UV shop-lights and tubes.

crossing_safe_for_guests.description: Whether a Guest can cross without taking light-injury.

arc.start_state: An ordinary night street with neon thin and no UV cage.
arc.end_state: A corridor of shop-lights Hale must cross already hungry.

b01.text: A narrow Main Street diner with a counter, six booths, and a front window on the crossing.

b02.text: The last booth sits farthest from the door and nearest the kitchen radio.

b03.text: A register and a coffee can of tips live by the front, under a clip for notes.

b01.text: Coffee, grill fat, a warm radio, and the particular quiet of three in the morning.

b02.text: Glitches, when they come, climb the front glass as a roll-bar, never as a menu.

b01.text: Cora holds the keys after eleven; Al is a name on the license.
Open all night at t0; later she can lock it after dark.
It is the room where hours are poured, recorded, returned, and finally clipped.
The diner has always been the town's night clock, even for Hosts who lose the night.

after_dark_policy.description: Whether the diner still receives night customers.

register_display.description: What is clipped at the register beside the tip can.

window_artifact.description: Analog glitch visible on the front glass.

arc.start_state: An open graveyard diner with a radio, a tip can, and no one's face on the register.
arc.end_state: A locked archive: his developing Polaroid at the clip, tape hissing, a roll-bar on the glass.

b01.text: A deep Main Street shop of aisles, a mezzanine office, and rooms above where Tom sleeps.

b02.text: UV tubes stand in a back rack beside shop-lights and extension cord.

b01.text: Oil, sawdust, and a bell on the door that sounds too loud after ten.
Tom locks the front and will still open for cash at the side.
Posted hours end at six; after-hours is a knock and a name.
Tools, tubes, and the invoice that will point at the dawn site come from here.
The shop has sold the same fasteners to the same families for a generated generation.

uv_stock.description: Sellable UV tubes and shop-lights remaining.

after_hours_open.description: Whether Tom will still unbolt the side door.

arc.start_state: A fully stocked hardware store whose back rack has not yet armed the town.
arc.end_state: The source of Kerr's maze, Cora's lamp, and the invoice that names the stone.

b01.text: A low brick hospital at the north end of town with a night entrance and a blood store.
Disinfectant, shoe squeak, a vending machine that never quite fills.
Night staff hold the floor; Holtz intends to hold the pints.
The night door takes a badge or a convincing emergency.
It is Denise's floor, a planned feed, and the first tap Holtz will dry.
The building has always been the town's official night, complete with charts that reset.

blood_stores.description: Availability of banked blood and easy clinical access.

night_access.description: How a Guest without a badge gets onto the floor.

arc.start_state: A stocked night hospital with a door that still opens to a good story.
arc.end_state: A dry ward under tribute talk, pushing Hale's hunger onto remaining Hosts.

b01.text: A programmed stand of pine and maple west of town, fog thicker between trunks.

b02.text: The treeline is visible from the last streetlight and then is not.

b01.text: Wet needles, no birds after dark, a wrongness that is analog rather than gothic.
Ur-Vampires own the deep paths; Wynn intends to own one of their hearts.
Anyone may walk in; not everyone walks out with a pulse.
One heartless body here will tell the town the woods are a hunt.
The woods were written as a risk tax on Guests who get bored of streets.

body_at_treeline.description: Whether a heartless Ur-Vampire corpse is visible from the last light.

arc.start_state: An unused hunting ground with no corpse to announce it.
arc.end_state: A treeline that holds one heartless body and then stays off-screen.

b01.text: A standing memorial stone in the Old First churchyard at the east edge of town.

b02.text: A stained church window faces the stone and takes flash like a wrong hour of day.

b03.text: Dawn hits the face of the stone first, then the grass, then the last shade by the wall.

b01.text: Wet granite, cut grass, a clock in the steeple that does not need to be right.
No Guest holds it at t0; invocation here is the only legal win.
Ungated. UV tubes can be dragged up the path. Shade lasts only until the sun clears the wall.
The Ritual ends here or does not end, and the match follows that fact.
The stone was placed as a Revolutionary marker and rewritten as the only dawn altar.

sun_on_stone.description: Whether dawn light has taken the face of the stone.

uv_encroaching.description: Whether shop-lights or tubes are being dragged onto the path.

tokens_present.description: Whether the assembled tokens are at the site, and in whose hands.

arc.start_state: An unused churchyard stone whose function Hale has not yet decoded.
arc.end_state: A dawn altar where the invocation is withheld and sun takes a hand instead of a winner.

b01.text: Every outbound road softens into fog and returns the driver to the same mile marker.
The fog reads as weather until it reads as static; neither can be driven through.
The match owns the loop; no Guest or Host can author an exit here.
You may enter the fog; you will not leave town.
It is why Cora's bus money is a story and why Hale cannot walk away.
The loop is the closed-match rule wearing a county road.

closed.description: Whether the road still returns everyone to town; ending needs it true.

fog_read.description: How the limit presents to the eye.

arc.start_state: A fogged county road that already loops and still looks like weather.
arc.end_state: The same closed road after sunrise, still looping, now reading closer to static.

b01.text: A hill campus of clapboard houses and a green that holds parties after dark.
Record players, cheap wine, students who stay up as if dawn were a rumor.
Nico intends to own the houses by invitation.
Open to anyone who looks like they were invited.
Willing donors here rewrite where blood still flows in town.
The campus is period texture with real emotional models inside the students.

cult_visible.description: Whether a standing group of willing donors is obvious on campus.

arc.start_state: An ordinary hill campus with parties but no cult.
arc.end_state: An off-screen reservoir of willing throats that changes the town's blood map.

b01.text: She bought it used with two weeks of tips and will not sell it back.
A battered SX-70 with a strap worn dark where it crosses her chest.
It makes a physical frame that sleep cannot take.
It is her claim that a night happened.
It lives on her body during shift and on the diner shelf at close.
She started shooting empty rooms so the town could not deny itself later.

arc.start_state: A used Polaroid on a waitress's strap, film unspent on any Guest.
arc.end_state: The instrument that put his face in a stack the wipe cannot cancel.

b01.text: Cora has been adding dated frames of empty rooms and streets for months of her model-life.
A rubber-banded sheaf of Polaroids with pencil dates on the backs.
It carries facts across wipes and will catch Ritual residue Hale cannot otherwise see.
It is the thing that cannot be reset once his face is in it.
She keeps it under the register in a tin that used to hold tea.
The earliest frames are empty-diner proofs for a departure that has not come.

b02.text: One early unremarked frame will include the careful man who paid and tipped.

frame_count.description: Number of Polaroids in the sheaf.

content_flag.description: Highest-stakes content the stack has acquired.

arc.start_state: A small sheaf of empty-room proofs with no Guest in them.
arc.end_state: The continuous self she keeps, holding ritual streets and a still-wet picture of his face.

b01.text: A drugstore tape Cora bought to record last songs off the diner radio.
A C-90 in a cracked plastic case, spine labeled in block ink.
It will hold missing hours and, later, Hale's calm instructions from a feed.
A voice that can be replayed after sleep is a kind of justice she can carry.
It lives in her apron until it lives in her hands at the stone.
At t0 it holds one last song and a stretch of blank tape.

track.description: What a playback would currently give.

arc.start_state: A drugstore tape with one radio song and a blank remainder.
arc.end_state: The hours she kept, handed back at the stone, run out to hiss beside the register.

b01.text: Four locatable pieces written into the town; they cannot be spawned or wished.

b02.text: Residue of them already exists as chalk, a wrong-hour window, tubes, and a site photo.

b01.text: Small period objects that do not look holy until they are gathered at the stone.
Held together at dawn, they permit one invocation that ends the match for that Guest.
They are mastery in a pocket, and later a debt she can hide.
They begin scattered; none are in a Guest's hands.
The match placed them where a mapper and a photographer might both trip over them.

assembled.description: How many of the four tokens have been located and gathered.

holder.description: Who currently controls the gathered set.

arc.start_state: Four unfound pieces scattered through a town that does not know they are a key.
arc.end_state: A complete set hidden by Cora, denying every Guest a winner.

b01.text: A display shop-light from Briggs, sold as a sanitizing lamp.
A metal-caged tube on a short cord, brutal when lit.
It injures Guests; Cora can carry it to the stone.
A work light used as a boundary she finally draws.
It begins on Tom's back rack.
Kerr will empty the rack for a maze; one lamp can still walk.

holder.description: Who currently has the portable lamp.

arc.start_state: An unlit sanitizing lamp on a hardware rack.
arc.end_state: The lamp in Cora's hand at the stone, ready to burn him rather than lose the night.

b01.text: Tom's invoice pad; the relevant sheet does not yet exist as a filled form.
Yellow carbon paper, a heavy hand, a delivery note that can name a churchyard.
Once issued, it points at the dawn site through where the tubes were sent.
A receipt that does the work of a map.
Blank in the mezzanine; later it can enter Cora's tin.
Tom writes every bulk sale because that is how his father kept the shop honest.

issued.description: Whether the UV delivery has been written down.

holder.description: Who currently has the filled invoice.

arc.start_state: A blank invoice pad in a hardware mezzanine.
arc.end_state: A filled carbon in the archive that helped name the stone.

b01.text: A coffee can Cora labeled TIPS in marker and keeps beside the register.
A blue can, torn label, bills folded small enough to hide.
It is her bus money and later the neighbor of his clipped Polaroid.
The old want sitting beside the new memory.
It does not leave the diner.
She has been feeding it instead of herself for a departure the road will not allow.

polaroid_clipped_beside.description: Whether the developing Polaroid of Hale is clipped beside the can.

arc.start_state: A coffee can of bus money with no photograph beside it.
arc.end_state: The same can after sunrise, his still-wet face clipped to the register beside it.

b01.text: It does not exist at t0; it will be taken from a night she may not remember shooting.
A white-bordered frame of a forgettable man who stops being forgettable once kept.
It is the plant that cannot be reset: his cover in chemical form.
Recognition made small enough to clip to a register.
Unshot. Later it can be returned, stolen, or clipped.
An earlier unremarked frame will first catch him as furniture; this one is the face.

exists.description: Whether the frame has been shot.

holder.description: Who holds the frame once it exists.

arc.start_state: An unshot frame.
arc.end_state: A still-developing picture of his face clipped to the diner register after sunrise.

b01.text: Six vampires spawned into the closed match: Hale, Anja, Kerr, Holtz, Nico, and Wynn.
There is no agreed leader; the Ritual admits one winner.
Each wants the single prize; their methods do not require them to meet.
Period clothes, one hundred dollars each, hunger, and whatever the town will give.
Cohesion is zero; interference is how they touch.
They bought tickets from an extra-diegetic underclass and cannot log out.

arc.start_state: Six uneliminated Guests, none holding tokens.
arc.end_state: A match still running with no winner declared and Hale still inside it.

b01.text: Cora Voss, Tom Briggs, and Denise Cole: the three Hale chose to drain short of death.
No hierarchy; Cora will become the one who compares notes first.
They want their nights to add up and their jobs to hold.
Keys, bruises, invoices, Polaroids, and the habit of working when others sleep.
Low at t0; shared gaps will raise it.
They already share the town's night economy without sharing a secret.

comparing_notes.description: Whether the three have begun matching gaps across jobs.

rotation_viable.description: Whether Hale can still feed this set cleanly.

arc.start_state: Three unconnected night workers with full blood and clean wipes.
arc.end_state: A small waking network whose locks and notes close Hale's clean rotation.

b01.text: Campus Hosts Nico gathers into a standing circle of given throats.
Nico at the center by charm, not by title.
They want belonging and a night that feels chosen.
Houses, record players, and bodies that reset.
High while the parties last; a wipe makes the yes cheap.
The circle does not exist at spawn.

formed.description: Whether the cult exists as a standing group.

arc.start_state: No cult, only a campus that stays up late.
arc.end_state: An off-screen flock that relocates the town's available blood.

b01.text: Holtz plus the night badges and ward keys he can hold.
Holtz sets terms; Hosts repeat them as rumor.
Monopolize stored blood and sell access as tribute.
The hospital store, implied police nights, and fear of dry wards.
Cohesion is scarcity, not loyalty.
The network is a Guest tactic, not a preexisting mafia.

arc.start_state: No tribute talk, wards still stocked.
arc.end_state: An off-screen monopoly that dries the hospital and alters midgame hunger.

b01.text: A finite set of four tokens and one spoken invocation at the Founders' Stone at dawn.

b02.text: Completion makes that Guest immune to sun and ends the match in their favor.

b03.text: Ending the match is a wipe with no morning after for any analog stack.

b01.text: Every Guest treats it as the only paying exit; Hosts do not know its name.
It is a match rule, not a religion, and it will not bend for sympathy.
Spoken, it crowns a winner and erases the board; withheld, the match keeps running.
Hale came in already hunting it; decoding it is the external plot.

decoded_by_hale.description: How completely Hale understands site, tokens, and the match-end cost.

invocation_spoken.description: Whether any Guest has spoken the dawn words.

match_running.description: Whether the closed match is still in play.

arc.start_state: A rumored win condition with tokens unfound and the match running.
arc.end_state: A fully decoded ritual that is not spoken, leaving the match running with no winner.

b01.text: Every time a Host sleeps, autobiographical memory since the previous waking is erased.

b02.text: Semantic skill and personality persist; affective residue and somatic marks bleed through.

b03.text: Facts do not persist unless an analog object carries them.

b01.text: Hosts experience it as ordinary sleep; Guests treat it as infrastructure.
It is the designed failsafe against existential collapse.
Intact, it keeps the town renewable; torn, fragments walk around and compare notes.
It was written to protect models from realizing the frame.

integrity.description: How completely Host sleep still erases the night.

arc.start_state: An intact failsafe: sleep takes every Host night cleanly.
arc.end_state: A torn failsafe that leaves fragments, voices, and a face no morning can cancel.

b01.text: It requires both Anja's stacked writes and Hale's rotational drains of the same three Hosts.

b02.text: Either alone is insufficient.

b03.text: After it tears, wipes go incomplete and Hosts can compare notes.

b04.text: It manifests as analog artifact, never as a menu.

b01.text: No one names it; they meet it as a Polaroid they do not remember taking.
It has no priest; it is an accident of two competent methods.
It is the mandatory bridge from the game plot to the town waking.
It is latent at spawn because the conjunction has not yet been run.

phase.description: Progress of the conjunction from latent to a spreading tear.

arc.start_state: A latent conjunction: writes not stacked, rotation not yet run.
arc.end_state: A spreading tear that lets a town keep hours and a face.

b01.text: If a Host reaches a stable, evidence-backed belief that they are inside a simulation, the model breaks.

b02.text: Breakage is catatonia, uncontrolled affect, or self-destruction.

b03.text: Analog cover can hold facts without forcing the forbidden belief.

b01.text: Cora fears going crazy more than she fears a man; this is that fear's real name.
It is a hard engine rule, not a metaphor.
It keeps philosophy off the dialogue and on the objects.
The wipe exists because this threshold does.

town_risk.description: How close the waking Hosts are to a simulation-belief break.

arc.start_state: A distant threshold no Host is near, because no Host has evidence.
arc.end_state: A live risk Cora evades by keeping analog hours instead of a theory.
